question:
**Case Study 9 (Cryptography – Encoding/Decoding Cycles):**

Consider three encoding functions on $S = \mathbb{R}$:

* $f(x) = x + 2$

* $g(x) = 3x$

* $h(x) = x^2$

(a) Compute $f \circ g$ and $g \circ f$ explicitly and state whether $f$ and $g$ commute under composition.

(b) Assuming $k(x) = x^2$ (i.e., $h$), is there any order of function composition among $f, g, h$ such that the resulting function is one-one?

(c) If $p(x) = x^2$ and $q(x) = \sqrt{x}$ with suitable domains so compositions make sense, is $p \circ q$ an identity? Prove.
explanation:
(a)

$f \circ g(x) = f(g(x)) = f(3x) = 3x + 2$

$g \circ f(x) = g(f(x)) = g(x+2) = 3(x+2) = 3x + 6$

So, $f$ and $g$ **do not commute** under composition: $f \circ g \neq g \circ f$.

(b)

Any composition involving $h(x)$ or $k(x) = x^2$ will generally not be one-one, as $x^2$ is not injective on $\mathbb{R}$. Compose in any order; the square means $x$ and $-x$ have same image, so overall function will not be one-one except possibly if domain is restricted to $x \geq 0$.

(c)

$p \circ q(x) = p(q(x)) = (\sqrt{x})^2 = x$ for $x \geq 0$.

So, $p \circ q$ is the identity on $[0, \infty)$. Verified.

options.A:
(a) $(f\circ g)(x)=3x+2$ and $(g\circ f)(x)=3x+6$, so $f$ and $g$ do not commute.
(b) Any composition involving $h(x)=x^2$ is not one-one on $\mathbb{R}$ in general; one-one behaviour needs suitable domain restriction such as $x\ge0$.
(c) $(p\circ q)(x)=(\sqrt{x})^2=x$ for $x\ge0$, so it is the identity on $[0,\infty)$.
options.B:
(a) $(f\circ g)(x)=(g\circ f)(x)=3x+2$, so $f$ and $g$ commute.
(b) Every composition involving $h$ is one-one on $\mathbb{R}$.
(c) $p\circ q$ is not defined for $x\ge0$.
options.C:
(a) $(f\circ g)(x)=3x+6$ and $(g\circ f)(x)=3x+2$, so they commute.
(b) Only $h\circ h$ is one-one.
(c) $p\circ q(x)=x^2$.
options.D:
(a) $(f\circ g)(x)=x+5$ and $(g\circ f)(x)=x+6$.
(b) No function composition is possible.
(c) $p\circ q$ is identity on all real numbers.
